newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON ALMOST ELIMINATED FROM WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON ALMOST ELIMINATED FROM WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson almost crashed out of the world championships on Sunday when he badly misjudged the final metres in the second round of the men's 400.
The Olympic 200 and 400 metres champion slowed too drastically in the final 10 metres of the race , allowing Senegal's Ibrahima Wade to snatch third place on the line.

Only the top three finishers from each of the four heats were guaranteed a place in the semifinals and Johnson had to wait until the end of the fourth heat before knowing that he had gone through to Monday's semifinals as one of the four fastest losers.
Johnson looked relaxed as he hit the final bend and started looking around him down the home straight as well as slowing down when Wade suddenly emerged on his right.
Britain's Jamie Baulch won the race in 45.06 seconds ahead of Uganda's Davis Kamoga (45.25) with Wade clocking 45.38, one hundredth of a second faster than Johnson.
"I was sure I had a firm grip with my position and I just didn't see him come up," Johnson said. "It surprised me that he was suddenly right beside me."

Earlier Johnson made a comfortable start to his campaign in front of a tiny morning crowd with an easy victory in his first round heat in 45.66. He said afterwards that he wanted to conserve as much as energy as he could in qualifying for the final.
Johnson was allowed to compete in Athens after the rules of the competition were changed to allow defending champions the automatic right to compete.

The 29-year-old American, who also completed a 200 and 400 double at the last world championships in Gothenburg in 1995, was not selected for the U.S. team after failing to compete in the national trials because of a thigh injury sustained in a 150 metres clash with Olympic 100 champion Donovan Bailey.
